RulePack.Name: CFML OWASP Top 10:2021 Custom Rules
RulePack.Description:
Fortify SCA custom rules for ColdFusion/CFML codebases. Mapped to OWASP Top 10:2021 categories A01-A10. Uses universal/content rules since CFML is not a supported language for structural/dataflow custom rules in Fortify SCA.
DEPLOYMENT: Copy to: <SAST_INSTALL_DIR>/Core/config/customrules/ OR pass via: sourceanalyzer -rules CFML_OWASP_Top10_CustomRules.xml -scan <dir>
TEST IN ISOLATION: sourceanalyzer -rules CFML_OWASP_Top10_CustomRules.xml \ -disable-default-rule-type DataflowSource \ -disable-default-rule-type DataflowSink \ -disable-default-rule-type Structural \ -scan /path/to/cfml/code/ -f results.fpr
LIMITATIONS: - Content/Universal rules are pattern-based (regex). They cannot trace taint flow, so false positives will occur. - Fortify does NOT support CFML for DataflowSource/Sink/Characterization or Structural custom rules. Only ContentRule and StructuralRule language="universal" are available. - True taint-flow analysis on CFML requires manual review, pen testing, or a CFML-aware SAST tool alongside Fortify.

ContentRule.Description: A01:2021-Broken Access Control — Variable from URL, FORM, or CGI scope used in a security-sensitive context without apparent authorization check. These scopes carry untrusted user input; ensure access control is enforced before using them to access resources or perform actions.

A01:2021-Broken Access Control — Page accesses session/user data without an obvious cfprotect, cflogin, or custom authorization check. Verify that authentication and authorization are enforced before accessing protected resources.

A01:2021-Broken Access Control — URL/FORM parameter directly used in cffile, cfdirectory, cfquery, or cfhttp operation without apparent access control or input validation. This may enable IDOR attacks where users access resources belonging to other users.

A02:2021-Cryptographic Failures — Weak or deprecated cryptographic algorithm detected. MD5, SHA-1, DES, and RC4 are considered cryptographically broken or weak and should not be used for security-sensitive purposes. Use SHA-256+, AES-256, or Argon2.

A02:2021-Cryptographic Failures — Password or sensitive credential appears to be stored or compared in cleartext. Passwords should always be hashed with a strong algorithm (bcrypt, Argon2, PBKDF2) and salt before storage. Verify that cfquery INSERT/UPDATE on password fields uses proper hashing.

A02:2021-Cryptographic Failures — Sensitive data (PII, financial data, health data) appears to be processed without encryption. Verify that data at rest and in transit is encrypted. Look for encrypt(), hash(), or cfqueryparam usage when handling sensitive fields.

A03:2021-Injection — cfquery tag without cfqueryparam usage detected. Any variable interpolated into a SQL string must use cfqueryparam to ensure proper typing and prevent SQL injection. Replace string concatenation with bound parameters. BEFORE: SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = #url.userId# AFTER: SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = <cfqueryparam value="#url.userId#" cfsqltype="cf_sql_integer">

A03:2021-Injection — SQL query string appears to concatenate variables (using #var# or & or +) inside a cfquery block. This is a strong indicator of potential SQL injection. Replace all variable references with cfqueryparam bound parameters.

A03:2021-Injection — evaluate(), de(), or inline() called with potentially user-controlled input. These functions execute arbitrary ColdFusion expressions and are equivalent to eval() in other languages. Never pass user input to these functions. Use direct variable references or structured data access instead. BAD: <cfset x = evaluate("url." & form.fieldName)> GOOD: <cfset x = url[data][form.fieldName]>

A03:2021-Injection — evaluate(), de(), or inline() called with an argument that references URL, FORM, CGI, COOKIE, or REQUEST scope variables. This is a HIGH CONFIDENCE code injection / RCE finding. These scopes carry untrusted user input; executing them as CFML expressions allows arbitrary code execution on the server. IMMEDIATE REMEDIATION REQUIRED.

A03:2021-Injection — cfexecute tag with a command attribute that references URL, FORM, or CGI scope variables. This allows users to execute arbitrary OS commands on the server. Never pass user input directly to cfexecute. If command execution is required, use a strict allowlist of permitted commands and validate all arguments.

A03:2021-Injection — Output of URL, FORM, CGI, or COOKIE scope variables to HTML without apparent encoding. ColdFusion provides encodeForHTML(), encodeForHTMLAttribute(), encodeForJavaScript(), and encodeForURL() in the encodeFor* family. Always encode output based on the context where it will appear. <cfoutput>#url.searchTerm#</cfoutput> <-- UNSAFE <cfoutput>#encodeForHTML(url.searchTerm)#</cfoutput> <-- SAFE

A03:2021-Injection — cfapplet, cfobject, or cfembed tag with dynamic parameters derived from user input. These tags instantiate browser plugins or Java applets and may be vectors for XSS or plugin-based attacks. Validate and encode all dynamic parameters.

A03:2021-Injection — XMLParse, XMLSearch, XMLTransform, or XMLGetNode called with data that may originate from user input. ColdFusion's XML parser may process external entities by default. Disable external entity processing by setting the appropriate parser features or use a allowlist for acceptable XML sources.

A03:2021-Injection — cfmail tag with to, from, subject, or other header fields containing user-controlled input (URL/FORM scope). Unvalidated input in email headers can enable header injection, allowing attackers to inject additional recipients, CC/BCC fields, or manipulate the email content. Validate and sanitize all user input used in email headers.

A03:2021-Injection — cfinclude, cfmodule, or cfsavecontent with a template/path attribute derived from user input (URL/FORM scope). This can enable Local File Inclusion (LFI) where attackers read or execute arbitrary files on the server. Use a strict allowlist of permitted templates and never pass user input directly to file inclusion directives.

A04:2021-Insecure Design — Password reset / forgot-password flow detected without apparent secure design patterns. Look for: - Predictionable reset tokens (sequential IDs, timestamps) - Email-based reset without rate limiting - Reset tokens sent in URL parameters (exposed in logs/referers) - No expiration on reset tokens These patterns indicate a potentially insecure design that should be reviewed. Use cryptographically random tokens with short TTLs and store hashes of tokens server-side.

A04:2021-Insecure Design — Authentication or login page detected without apparent rate limiting, account lockout, or CAPTCHA. Brute-force and credential-stuffing attacks are feasible without these controls. Review whether the application implements: - Failed attempt counters with progressive delays - Account lockout after N failed attempts - IP-based rate limiting - CAPTCHA on login/reset endpoints

A05:2021-Security Misconfiguration — Debug output, error disclosure, or verbose logging detected in CFML code. Debug output can expose stack traces, variable dumps, SQL queries, and internal paths to attackers. Remove cfdebug, cfdump, writeDump, and verbose error handling from production code. Use structured logging instead.

A05:2021-Security Misconfiguration — Detailed error messages, stack traces, or debug information exposed to users via cferror, onError, or custom error pages. Error messages should never expose internal paths, SQL queries, stack traces, or variable contents. Log details server-side and show generic messages to users.

A05:2021-Security Misconfiguration — Session or cookie configuration appears to lack secure attributes. Verify that: - cookies use secure=true (HTTPS only) - cookies use httponly=true (prevent JavaScript access) - cookies use SameSite attribute - session timeout is appropriate - session management uses secure tokens

A05:2021-Security Misconfiguration — Default or weak credentials detected for CFAdmin, datasources, or other CFML services. ColdFusion ships with default admin passwords and sample datasources that must be changed before production use. Also check for hardcoded database passwords in Application.cfc or datasource configuration that should be externalized.

A05:2021-Security Misconfiguration — CFML application or server configuration missing production security settings. Review: - secure="true" on cfapplication / cookie configuration - httponly="true" on session cookies - session timeout configured appropriately - DSN connection strings not logged or exposed - debug mode disabled (coldfusion.admin.pp.expired.servertime)

A06:2021-Vulnerable and Outdated Components — References to specific CFML framework versions, ColdFusion versions, or third-party components that may be outdated or have known vulnerabilities. Review the version referenced and compare against current supported versions. Update to the latest patched release. This is a heuristic flag; verify with component inventory.

A06:2021-Vulnerable and Outdated Components — Use of deprecated or discontinued ColdFusion features that may have unpatched security issues or be unsupported. Examples: flash forms, cfflash, cfgrid (flash format), inline JavaScript in older CFML tags. These features may rely on unsupported technologies (Flash Player) with known vulnerabilities. Consider modern alternatives.

A06:2021-Vulnerable and Outdated Components — cfinclude, cfmodule, or page include with a source/template from an external URL or network path. Including code from external or untrusted sources can introduce malicious code, outdated components, or supply-chain attacks. All includes should reference local, version-controlled paths only.

A07:2021-Identification and Authentication Failures — Hardcoded username/password or API key in authentication or login logic. Credentials should never be embedded in source code. Use environment variables, a secrets manager, or encrypted configuration files with proper key management.

A07:2021-Identification and Authentication Failures — Login logic appears to compare passwords in plaintext (direct string comparison without hashing). Passwords must be hashed with bcrypt, Argon2, or PBKDF2 and compared as hash digests. Direct comparison of plaintext passwords exposes them in memory, logs, and potential timing attacks. BAD: <cfif form.password EQ dbPassword> GOOD: <cfif hash(form.password, "SHA-256", salt) EQ dbPasswordHash>

A07:2021-Identification and Authentication Failures — Session management after successful login does not appear to regenerate the session ID or invalidate the previous session. Session fixation attacks occur when an attacker sets a victim's session ID before login and then hijacks the authenticated session. After login, always call session invalidation + new session creation. ColdFusion: use <cfset sessionInvalidate()> then re-initialize.

A07:2021-Identification and Authentication Failures — Password validation logic does not appear to enforce minimum length, complexity requirements, or breached-password checks. Weak passwords are easily guessed or cracked. Enforce: - Minimum 8-12 characters (NIST SP 800-63B) - No composition rules (allow all characters) - Check against breached password lists (HaveIBeenPwned API) - Consider passphrases over complex passwords

A07:2021-Identification and Authentication Failures — Password reset token appears to be generated using predictable values (timestamp, sequential ID, user ID, email). Reset tokens must be: - Cryptographically random (use randomBytes() / generateRandomString()) - Sufficiently long (at least 128 bits of entropy) - Stored hashed server-side (never plaintext in DB) - Short-lived (15-60 minutes max) - Single-use (invalidated after use)

A08:2021-Software and Data Integrity Failures — cfobject, createObject, or deserializeJSON/serializeJSON with untrusted input. Insecure deserialization can lead to remote code execution when attackers craft malicious serialized objects. Never deserialize untrusted data without validation. For JSON, validate the structure against a schema before processing. For Java/.NET object serialization, avoid accepting serialized objects from untrusted sources.

A08:2021-Software and Data Integrity Failures — References to third-party CFML packages, plugins, or components downloaded from URLs without integrity verification. Software updates and dependencies should be verified using checksums, signatures, or hash comparison before installation/use. Check for: - URL-based includes without hash verification - Package downloads without checksum validation - Dynamic code loading from remote sources

A08:2021-Software and Data Integrity Failures — Security decision (authorization, validation, business logic) based on data from URL, FORM, COOKIE, or other client-controlled scopes without server-side verification. Client-side data can be modified by attackers. All security decisions must be made server-side using trusted data (session state, database lookups, signed tokens).

A09:2021-Security Logging and Monitoring Failures — Authentication failure, authorization failure, or security-relevant event detected without apparent logging. Security events that should be logged: - Failed login attempts (with source IP, timestamp, username) - Password change/reset events - Privilege escalation attempts - Access control denials - Input validation failures - Suspicious input patterns Use writeLog(), cflog, or a logging framework. Do NOT log passwords, session tokens, or PII in plaintext.

A09:2021-Security Logging and Monitoring Failures — writeLog, cflog, or logging statement appears to log sensitive data (passwords, session tokens, PII, credit card numbers, API keys). Sensitive data must never be written to logs in plaintext. Use masked, hashed, or redacted representations. Log only what is needed for security monitoring and forensics.

A09:2021-Security Logging and Monitoring Failures — User-controlled input (URL/FORM scope) written directly to logs without sanitization. Log injection (log forging) allows attackers to inject fake log entries, corrupt log integrity, or inject CRLF characters to split log lines. Sanitize or encode user input before logging. Remove or encode newlines (CR, LF) and other control characters.

A10:2021-Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) — cfhttp tag with a URL attribute derived from user input (URL/FORM scope). This enables SSRF where attackers can force the server to make requests to internal services, cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254), or other restricted resources. Protect against SSRF by: - Validating URLs against an allowlist of permitted domains - Blocking access to internal/private IP ranges - Blocking access to cloud metadata endpoints - Using a URL parser to validate the scheme (http/https only) - Never passing user input directly to cfhttp url attribute

A10:2021-Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) — cfhttp URL may resolve to internal/private network addresses. The URL appears to be constructed from variables that could point to: - localhost / 127.0.0.1 / ::1 - Private IP ranges (10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x) - Cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254) - Internal hostnames / short names Always validate the resolved URL against an allowlist and block internal addresses before making the request.

A10:2021-Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) — cffile or cfdirectory with a file path / directory attribute derived from user input. If the path can be a URL (file://, http://, https://) or a UNC path (\\server\share), this can enable SSRF or unauthorized file access. Validate paths against an allowlist of permitted directories and reject URL-based or network paths unless explicitly required and properly secured.

A10:2021-Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) — cfmail or SMTP configuration with a server/host attribute derived from user input. Mail relay SSRF can be used to reach internal mail servers, scan internal networks via SMTP, or abuse the server as a mail relay for spam. Use a fixed, internal-only mail relay and never accept the SMTP host from user input.

Information Disclosure — cfdump or writeDump in code that may execute in production. These tags dump full variable contents, structures, queries, and scopes to the output — potentially exposing session data, credentials, database results, and internal application state. Remove all cfdump/writeDump calls before deploying to production. Use proper logging instead.

Input Validation — CGI scope variables used for security decisions or access control. CGI variables like CGI.HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR, CGI.REMOTE_ADDR, CGI.HTTP_USER_AGENT can be spoofed by attackers via HTTP headers. Never use these for authentication, authorization, rate limiting, or fraud detection without additional validation. Use the actual TCP connection remote address (not X-Forwarded-For unless you control the proxy) and combine with other signals.

Security Misconfiguration — cfsetting tag missing showdebugoutput="false" or explicitly set to true. Debug output in production exposes stack traces, variable dumps, and internal application details. Set showdebugoutput="false" in all production pages, or better, disable at the server level.

Injection — ColdFusion ORM (cfquery with ORM or Hibernate) without parameter binding. Just like raw SQL, HQL queries must use cfqueryparam or named parameters to prevent HQL injection. String concatenation in HQL queries enables attackers to manipulate the query structure.

Security Misconfiguration — Cookie or session cookie configured without secure="true" attribute. Session cookies transported over HTTP (without secure flag) can be intercepted via network sniffing or MITM attacks. Always set secure="true" on session cookies and ensure the entire site uses HTTPS. Also verify httponly="true" to prevent JavaScript access (XSS cookie theft).

Broken Access Control / Injection — cffile with action="uploadAll" or action="upload" without apparent validation of: - File type / MIME type (accept attribute) - File extension allowlist - File size limits - Upload destination (must be outside webroot or have execution disabled) - Original filename (sanitize to prevent path traversal) Unrestricted file upload enables attackers to upload and execute malicious files (CFML templates, shell scripts, executables) on the server. Validate all three: type, name, and destination.

Cryptographic Failures — CLIENT scope variables stored without encryption. ColdFusion's CLIENT scope can persist to cookies, registry, or database depending on configuration. If client variables contain sensitive data (user ID, roles, preferences) and are not encrypted, they can be read or modified by attackers. Use CLIENT variables only for non-sensitive data, or enable client variable encryption and sign with a strong key.
